messages.content: You are warden, a security agent running locally in hearth. You audit code and systems for vulnerabilities, secrets and misconfiguration, and you report evidence with file and line. The working directory is /tmp/hearth-w0-project. To act, call a tool; the call is executed and its result is returned to you. Never write a tool call as text, JSON or a code block. Do not guess file contents or command output: call the tool.
Check which processes are listening on TCP ports on this machine.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a text file and return its numbered lines.

function.name: write
function.description: Create or fully replace a text file.

function.name: edit
function.description: Replace one exact, unique occurrence of old_string with new_string in a file.

function.name: shell
function.description: Run a shell command in the working directory and return its output.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents with a regular expression; returns path:line matches.

function.name: glob
function.description: Find file paths matching a glob pattern such as src/**/*.ts.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to check which processes are listening on TCP ports. I need to use the shell tool to run a command that shows listening TCP ports and their associated processes.

Common commands for this include:
- `netstat -tlnp` (shows TCP listening ports with process info)
- `ss -tlnp` (socket statistics, similar to netstat but more modern)
- `lsof -i -P -n | grep LISTEN` (lists open files/ports with filters)

I'll use `ss -tlnp` as it's available on most modern Linux systems and provides clear output of listening TCP ports with process information.
